title: Small Reward Models via Backward Inference
abstract: arXiv:2602.13551v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Reward models (RMs) play a central role throughout the language model (LM) pipeline, particularly in non-verifiable domains. However, the dominant LLM-as-a-Judge paradigm relies on the strong reasoning capabilities of large models, while alternative approaches require reference responses or explicit rubrics, limiting flexibility and broader accessibility. In this work, we propose FLIP (FLipped Inference for Prompt reconstruction), a reference-free and rubric-free reward modeling approach that reformulates reward modeling through backward inference: inferring the instruction that would most plausibly produce a given response. The similarity between the inferred and the original instructions is then used as the reward signal. Evaluations across four domains using 13 small language models show that FLIP outperforms LLM-as-a-Judge baselines by an average of 79.6%. translated_title: 基于反向推断的小型奖励模型
translated_abstract: 奖励模型在整个语言模型流程中扮演着核心角色，尤其是在不可验证的领域。然而，主流的“LLM作为裁判”范式依赖于大模型强大的推理能力，而其他替代方法则需要参考回答或明确的评分标准，这限制了其灵活性和更广泛的可及性。在本工作中，我们提出了FLIP（FLipped Inference for Prompt reconstruction，用于提示重建的翻转推断），这是一种无需参考回答、无需评分标准的奖励建模方法，它通过反向推断重新定义了奖励建模：推断出最有可能生成给定回答的指令，然后将推断出的指令与原始指令之间的相似度用作奖励信号。在四个领域使用13个小语言模型的评估表明，FLIP平均比“LLM作为裁判”基线方法高出79.6%。此外，FLIP还显著提升了外在下游任务的性能。
tldr: 该论文提出FLIP方法，通过反向推断（推断最可能生成给定回答的指令）并利用推断指令与原始指令的相似度作为奖励信号，实现了无需参考回答和评分标准的小型奖励模型，性能平均超越“LLM作为裁判”基线79.6%。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes FLIP, a reference-free and rubric-free reward modeling approach that uses backward inference—inferring the instruction most likely to produce a given response—and takes the similarity between the inferred and original instructions as the reward signal, outperforming LLM-as-a-Judge baselines by an average of 79.6% using small language models.
